sketch: Estimate the mean of f:{0,..,N-1}->[0,1] via a phase-encoding / eigenvalue approach rather than amplitude estimation. Registers: index register (n qubits, N=2^n) and a precision register (m qubits). Step 1: prepare uniform superposition over x with Hadamards. Step 2: apply the diagonal phase oracle D = sum_x exp(2 pi i f(x)) |x><x| (compiled from the explicit classical table of f; this is a functional simulation, not a black-box query bound). Step 3: define U = H^{n} D H^{n}; then <0|U|0> = (1/N) sum_x exp(2 pi i f(x)), the mean of exp(2 pi i f). For small f (f in [0,eps]) this is approximately 1+2 pi i * mean(f) so the mean is read from the phase and amplitude of the overlap. Step 4: use a Hadamard-test-style control on U (or powers U^k with control qubits) to estimate the overlap; the control register is decoded by an inverse QFT to read the phase of the overlap. Reconstruction here is a distinct family from Grover-style amplitude estimation: it uses a phase-oracle expectation (Hadamard test / Fourier phase readout), in the spirit of the Aharonov-style variant mentioned in the abstract but not claimed to match it. Tiny instance: n=2, f=(0,0.05,0.1,0.05), compile D as diagonal phases, control qubit with Hadamard test, ancilla measurement probabilities give Re and Im of the overlap, from which mean f approx Im/(2 pi) for small f; the circuit omits measurement and outputs the unitary with control qubit. Limitations: this only achieves a narrower task; first-order small-f approximation is biased, with no optimal-query claim; the median algorithm over arbitrary distance functions is out of scope; the abstract's asymptotically optimal algorithm is not reconstructed.
